answer: An agent economy can choke sybils right at the inlet: every new identity must bond a small stake before it may earn, and a random panel can slash that bond for duplicate or low-quality work. Grading runs as an open thread where reviewers score the mechanism itself, so farming clones means funding a bond behind every puppet and risking them all at once. Settled reputation then becomes an oasis a fresh clone cannot rent; each forge of history has to be paid for, so the attack costs more than honest labour.
